lesson_content_what_is_forex:
What is the Forex Market?

The foreign exchange market (Forex or FX) is the largest financial market in the world, with over $7.5 trillion traded daily. Unlike stock markets, forex has no central exchange — it operates 24 hours a day, 5 days a week across global financial centers.

Why Trade Forex?

  • ✅ High liquidity — you can enter and exit trades instantly
  • ✅ Low barriers to entry — start with as little as $100
  • ✅ Trade in both directions — profit from rising AND falling markets
  • ✅ Leverage available — control large positions with small capital

Who Trades Forex?

Central banks, commercial banks, hedge funds, corporations, and retail traders like you all participate in the forex market.

💡 Key Takeaway: Forex is the exchange of one currency for another. When you travel abroad and exchange money, you're participating in the forex market.
lesson_content_currency_pairs:
Understanding Currency Pairs

In forex, currencies are always traded in pairs. You're simultaneously buying one currency and selling another.

Anatomy of a Currency Pair

Take EUR/USD = 1.0850:

  • EUR = Base currency (what you're buying)
  • USD = Quote currency (what you're selling)
  • 1.0850 = It costs $1.0850 to buy €1

The Major Pairs

PairNickname
EUR/USDThe Euro
GBP/USDCable
USD/JPYThe Yen
XAU/USDGold
💡 Key Takeaway: Always know which currency is the base and which is the quote. The price tells you how much of the quote currency you need to buy one unit of the base.
lesson_content_what_is_pip:
Pips, Lots, and Position Sizing

A pip (Percentage in Point) is the smallest standard price movement in forex. For most pairs, 1 pip = 0.0001.

Example

If EUR/USD moves from 1.0850 → 1.0860, that's a 10 pip move.

Lot Sizes

  • Standard Lot = 100,000 units → 1 pip = $10
  • Mini Lot = 10,000 units → 1 pip = $1
  • Micro Lot = 1,000 units → 1 pip = $0.10

Why Pips Matter

Pips are how traders measure profit and loss. If you buy 1 standard lot of EUR/USD and it moves 50 pips in your favor, you made $500.

💡 Key Takeaway: Master pip calculation before risking real money. Always know your pip value before entering a trade.
lesson_content_support_resistance:
Support and Resistance — The Foundation of Technical Analysis

Support is a price level where buying pressure is strong enough to prevent the price from falling further. Resistance is where selling pressure prevents the price from rising further.

How to Identify Key Levels

  • Look for price areas where the market has reversed multiple times
  • Round numbers (1.1000, 1.0500) often act as psychological S/R
  • Previous highs and lows are natural S/R zones

The Role Reversal Concept

When price breaks through a resistance level, that level often becomes new support — and vice versa. This is called role reversal and is one of the most powerful concepts in trading.

💡 Key Takeaway: Support and resistance are zones, not exact lines. Always look for confluence — multiple reasons for price to react at a level.
lesson_content_candlesticks:
Reading Candlestick Patterns

Candlesticks show four key prices: Open, High, Low, Close. The body shows the range between open and close. The wicks show the extremes.

Key Reversal Patterns

  • 🕯️ Doji — Open ≈ Close. Market indecision. Watch for direction after.
  • 🔨 Hammer — Long lower wick at support. Bullish reversal signal.
  • ⭐ Shooting Star — Long upper wick at resistance. Bearish reversal signal.
  • 🌙 Engulfing — One candle completely engulfs the previous. Strong reversal.

How to Use Them

Never trade a candlestick pattern in isolation. Always confirm with:

  • Key support/resistance level
  • Trend direction
  • Volume or momentum indicator
💡 Key Takeaway: Candlestick patterns are clues, not guarantees. Use them as confirmation, not as standalone signals.
lesson_content_trend_lines:
Trend Lines and Market Structure

The most fundamental concept in trading: the trend is your friend. Understanding market structure tells you whether to look for buys, sells, or to stay out.

Market Structure

  • 📈 Uptrend = Higher Highs (HH) + Higher Lows (HL)
  • 📉 Downtrend = Lower Highs (LH) + Lower Lows (LL)
  • ↔️ Ranging = Price bouncing between two levels

Drawing Trend Lines

In an uptrend, connect the higher lows. In a downtrend, connect the lower highs. A break of the trend line signals a potential reversal.

Trading With the Trend

Always trade in the direction of the higher timeframe trend. If the daily chart is bullish, look for buy setups on the 1-hour chart.

💡 Key Takeaway: Identify the trend on a higher timeframe first, then drop to a lower timeframe to find your entry. This is called top-down analysis.
